opencalls.title: Request for Proposals: 2027 Dewey Square Activation
opencalls.description: The Greenway Conservancy seeks an entrepreneurial partner to envision, design, build, install, manage, and operate a vibrant outdoor activation in Dewey Square Park. The activation may take the form of an outdoor concession, bar, kiosk, café, retail pop-up shop, market, activity, event or performance series, or other innovative concept that brings people together and enhances the experience of the plaza and surrounding district.

opencalls.title: Open Call: Public Art for Spatial Justice
opencalls.description: NEFA's Public Art for Spatial Justice grants range from $15,000 to $30,000 for up to a two-year grant period, starting March 2027. Projects must take place in Massachusetts and creatively cultivate expressions or embodiments of spatial justice through public art-making. All artistic disciplines are welcome to apply.

opencalls.title: Call for Art: Between Here & There
opencalls.description: “Between Here and There” is a multimedia exhibit presented by the Arlington Center for the Arts and Lexington Arts and Crafts Society. It brings these two artistic communities together with work from both youth and adults residing in both Arlington and Lexington as well as the Greater New England area.

opencalls.title: Open Call: Triennial's Public Art Accelerator
opencalls.description: The Triennial’s Public Art Accelerator returns with an open call for three experienced Greater Boston–based artists to be part of Cohort Ten of the Accelerator and the next Triennial in 2028. Workshops will run from March 2027 through June 2027 and will culminate in the inclusion of artist-driven proposals within the Triennial 2028 exhibition, set to open May 2028.

opencalls.title: Open Call: KIN
opencalls.description: This national exhibition, presented by Gallery 263 and juried by Nadirah Mansour, will examine the notion of kin beyond relationships of blood, culture, region, or circumstance. It asks what it means to become kin with those beyond humanity, how we understand them to be kin, and what our responsibilities toward kin who cannot speak or articulate needs is. Gallery 263 invites US-based artists of all experience levels to submit work that engages these questions and the material relationships they are enmeshed in.
